 Heard on ; 26.02.2026  Pronounced on : 06.03.2026  ORDER

Appellant - the Insurance Company has assailed the award dated 11- 04-2007 in this miscellaneous appeal, by which 5th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa decided the claim case No.72-2006 and allowed a compensation of Rs.2,26,583/- along with interest and cost of litigation, in favour of Respondent No.1, (hereinafter referred to as claimant), under the joint and several liability of appellant - Insurance Company in this property damage case.

entities.text: 5th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts in brief are that a petition was filed by claimant against owner, driver and Insurance Company of Truck No. HR-13-GA-0298 and they are respectively respondents No.2, 3 and 4 in this appeal.

Appellant was also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18070 2 MA-4193-2007 arrayed as respondent in claim petition, though it was the insurance company of the vehicle jeep which was being driven by claimant himself and who was also the owner of said jeep.
According to claimant, the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving on the part of truck driver.
Accordingly, a claim for Rs. 2,31,583/- for the damage of vehicle jeep caused on account of said accident was filed and the same was partially allowed by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal reached to the finding that accident occurred on account of negligence of drivers of both the vehicles and therefore, insurance companies of both the vehicles were held liable to pay the compensation amount under their joint and several liability.

The appeal has been preferred by the insurance company of vehicle jeep on the grounds that the driver of jeep being himself negligent for the accident to occur, cannot claim any amount for the damages against the insurer of jeep for being the first party.
It is further contended that no criminal case was registered against the jeep driver.
Therefore, the entire liability for paying compensation should be fixed upon the truck owner, driver and its insurance company and award imposing partial liability on appellant should be set aside.
4. Learned counsel for appellant-Insurance Company and also for respondent No.4, the insurance company of offending truck, were heard on the merits of the case.
Record of the Tribunal has been examined.
5. The impugned award reflects that the tribunal was of the opinion that on account of head-on collision between the two vehicles, both were liable for contributory negligence.

It is an admitted fact that no case of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18070 3 MA-4193-2007 negligent driving was registered against the driver of vehicle jeep, but tribunal, after appreciating the evidence and also the other material available on its record, came to the finding that there was contributory negligence on the part of drivers of both the vehicles.

Although, the percentage of contributory negligence was not defined specifically in the impugned award, but Para 14 of award conveys that the Tribunal was of the view that negligence was in proportion to 50% - 50%.
Admittedly, this finding has not been assailed either by respondent No.1-claimant or anyone from the rest of the respondents who were the truck owner, driver and its insurance company.

Thus, the finding of tribunal regarding 50% negligence on the part of truck driver and consequently 50% liability of its owner, driver and insurance company to pay the compensation amount has become final and need not to be examined in this appeal.
6. Now comes the question of the liability of appellant, the insurance company of vehicle jeep which was being driven by its owner, the insured.

Tribunal had arrived at a finding that owner-cum-driver of said jeep was liable to 50% extent for the accident to occur and said owner-cum-driver was the claimant before the Tribunal who did not challenge this finding given by tribunal against him.
A negligent driver cum owner, who is also the insured, cannot seek any compensation either under Section 163A or Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Such an owner-cum-driver is not a third party in relation to his own vehicle and therefore, cannot claim any compensation against his own insurance company for personal or property damage under the provision of either Section 163A or Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18070 4 MA-4193-2007 Reference may be made to the decision of Ram Khiladi and another v. United India Insurance Company and another (2020) 2 SCC 550 to strengthen this proposition.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Question may arise, what is the remedy available to the owner /insured to avail the benefit of insurance policy.
The answer lies in a claim for compensation under the own damage clause, if the insurance policy covers such a risk.

For this also, reference can be made to case laws of National United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Bhola Nath on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145995780/
2

sentences.text: Insurance Company Limited v. Ashalata Bhaumik in (2018) 9 SCC 801 and Dhanraj v. New India Assurance Company Limited in (2004) 8 SCC 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In terms of above discussion regarding facts and law, it is held that appellant/Insurance Company of vehicle Jeep is under no liability to pay compensation to claimant under the provision of Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act which was invoked by claimant before the tribunal.
9. Appeal is accordingly allowed and appellant - insurance company is discharged of any liability to pay compensation under the impugned award.

10. Let a copy of this order along with the record of the Tribunal be sent back to the concerned Tribunal for necessary compliance.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE
